title: Projection Operators (Select & SelectMany)
description: Learn to transform data using Select and flatten nested collections with SelectMany.

data.text: Projection operators transform elements in a collection into a new shape. LINQ provides two projection operators: **Select** and **SelectMany**.
The `Select` operator always returns an `IEnumerable` collection containing elements based on a transformation function. It is similar to the SELECT clause in SQL that produces a flat result set.
LINQ query syntax must end with a `Select` or `GroupBy` clause. The following example demonstrates the `Select` operator returning a collection of student names:

data.title: Select in Method Syntax

data.text: The `SelectMany` operator projects sequences of values based on a transform function and then flattens them into one sequence. This is useful for working with nested collections.

terms.definition: Transforms each element into a new shape. Returns one output element per input element.
Transforms each element into a sequence and flattens all sequences into one.
A type created on the fly with read-only properties, often used with Select for projections.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Select transforms each element into a new shape
Select can return anonymous types with custom properties
SelectMany flattens nested collections into a single sequence
Both operators are available in query and method syntax
data.takeaway: Continue to the next module to learn about sorting and grouping operators.
